# Aliasgar Khimani (@NovusEdge)

> Personal portfolio and writing by a systems architect in Finland. I build AI infrastructure, agent memory and decision-tracking tools, evals, systems software, and hardware projects.

Coding since 2013. My background is offensive security: CTFs, malware development, and pentesting. Much of my current work concerns what agents know, why they believe it, and which decisions should survive a new session.

Updated: 2026-09-12. These descriptions are an overview; consult the linked pages and repositories for current implementation details.

## Site directory

- [Home](https://novusedge.github.io/): Introduction and selected work.
- [About](https://novusedge.github.io/about/): Background, interests, and open-source contributions.

English is the default language. Localized routes use `/fi/` for Finnish, `/de/` for German, `/ja/` for Japanese, and `/zh/` for Simplified Chinese. Translation coverage varies by page. The three recent essays below are available in all five languages; for example, `/zh/blog/what-did-we-all-miss/`.

## Selected projects

- [Docket](https://novusedge.github.io/portfolio/docket/): Decision tracking for agents and complex agent workflows. Keeps settled choices, rejected options, and open questions outside the conversation, with supporting reasons and a history of superseded decisions. [Repository](https://github.com/NovusEdge/docket).
- [Engrammic](https://novusedge.github.io/portfolio/engrammic/): Epistemic memory for AI agents. Models claims, evidence, provenance, and decay so observations and beliefs can be traced to their sources. [Website](https://engrammic.ai), [repository](https://github.com/engrammic-ai/engrammic).
- [Veil](https://novusedge.github.io/portfolio/veil/): Persistent, sourced memory for agents, with memory decay and failed-approach history. [Repository](https://github.com/engrammic-ai/veil), [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@engrammic/veil).
- [Primitives](https://github.com/engrammic-ai/primitives): Python schemas and rules for observations, claims, facts, and beliefs. [Repository](https://github.com/engrammic-ai/primitives), [PyPI package](https://pypi.org/project/engrammic-primitives/).
- [stoat](https://novusedge.github.io/portfolio/stoat/): Local QEMU virtual machines on Linux, managed through a Go TUI and CLI. [Repository](https://github.com/NovusEdge/stoat).
- [ØCLOAK](https://novusedge.github.io/portfolio/ocloak/): A project exploring privacy infrastructure against mass surveillance, including RF/WiFi-sensing hardware and peer-to-peer threat intelligence. [Repository](https://github.com/NovusEdge/ocloak).
- [money-mesh](https://novusedge.github.io/portfolio/): An experimental autonomous-agent system with bounded budgets, node-owned business code, and a protected runtime. Self-sustaining operation is a design goal, not a claim of demonstrated profitability.
- [anti-slop](https://github.com/NovusEdge/anti-slop): A Claude Code plugin with prose rules, session hooks, and a linter for AI-written text. [Repository](https://github.com/NovusEdge/anti-slop).
- [goob](https://github.com/NovusEdge/goob): A Godot desktop pet that wanders, naps, and comments on desktop activity, with support for custom spritesheets. [Repository](https://github.com/NovusEdge/goob).
- [Palpatine](https://novusedge.github.io/portfolio/palpatine/): A tongue-in-cheek strategic-advisor plugin for pursuing goals. [Repository](https://github.com/NovusEdge/palpatine).

The portfolio distinguishes projects in development, shipped projects, older security work, and contributions to other projects. These labels do not establish production deployment, a release schedule, or activity in a particular week.

## Recent essays

- [What Did We All Miss?](https://novusedge.github.io/blog/what-did-we-all-miss/): September 12, 2026. Reflections on AI progress, research, robotics, and the gap between technical developments and public attention.
- [Google's €13 Billion in Finland](https://novusedge.github.io/blog/googles-13-billion-in-finland/): September 12, 2026. An essay on energy investment in Finland, grid constraints, and the attention given to generation versus storage.
- [Let's Talk About Plan A](https://novusedge.github.io/blog/plan-a-ai/): September 11, 2026. A broadly supportive critique of the AI Futures Project's AI 2040: Plan A, examining compute limits, transparency, verification, and constraints on AI systems.

## More writing

- [How Do You Know What's True?](https://novusedge.github.io/blog/epistemic-collapse/): The growing asymmetry between cheap generation and costly verification.
- [On Building Something... Engrammic](https://novusedge.github.io/blog/on-building-something-engrammic/): Why agent memory involves belief and evidence as well as retrieval.
- [All posts](https://novusedge.github.io/blog/): The published archive. Drafts are not part of this index.

## Earlier security work

Projects from the CTF and security-research years, including work with @AraChn3:

- [screenjack](https://github.com/ARaChn3/screenjack): Fullscreen takeover tooling.
- [hirejack](https://github.com/ARaChn3/hirejack): ATS security auditing.
- [prepender](https://github.com/ARaChn3/prepender): Executable infection research.
- [glowworm](https://github.com/ARaChn3/glowworm): Network worm research.
- [remy](https://github.com/ARaChn3/remy): Remote-access tooling with HTTP command and control.
- [Malware Dev Guide](https://github.com/NovusEdge/malware-development-guide): Community malware-development guide.
- [THM Writeups](https://github.com/NovusEdge/thm-writeups): TryHackMe CTF writeups.

## Collaboration and contact

I'm interested in agent memory, eval systems, multi-agent coordination, distributed systems, and hardware interfaces. For roles, I look for staff, founding, or research engineering work with technical depth and room to shape the problem. Remote, async-friendly small teams are a good fit. Open to the right contract or full-time opportunity.
